title: Intervention simulator & rollback playbook for LQ regressions from batching/cache config changes
creator: Marina Patel
description:
Purpose: build a repeatable simulator and a human-readable playbook that lets on-call and platform engineers evaluate intervention policies when configuration or model changes cause latency-vs-quality (LQ) regressions tied to batching and prefix/KV cache adjustments.

Scope: focused on config deltas that are frequently auto-tuned or rolled out (microbatch sizes, packing aggressiveness, prefix/KV TTLs, cache eviction aggressiveness, token aggregation heuristics). Not addressing model architecture or quantization changes in this ticket (separate orbit).

Goals:
- Produce a small suite of realistic perturbation scenarios and a synthetic workload harness that can inject config deltas and measure both latency distributions (P50/P95/P99), token-unit cost, and quality regressions using the Golden Prompt Bank (instruction-following, factuality checks, semantic similarity).
- Implement an "intervention simulator" that replays historical traffic slices against perturbed configs and evaluates rule-based policies (alert thresholds, automated scale-up, rollback to previous config, degrade-to-safe-model).
- Codify an on-call playbook with decision thresholds, confidence estimators, and recommended steps for automated rollback vs manual investigation.
- Surface false positive/negative rates for each policy using historical incidents and synthetic regressions.

Key components to deliver:
1) Perturbation scenarios: catalog of 12 targeted config changes (examples: microbatch +50%, microbatch -30%, KV TTL -80%, prefix cache disabled, packing factor +2, token aggregation disabled). Each scenario includes expected latency impact profile and hypothesized quality failure modes.
2) Workload harness: containerized generator (k8s job) that runs representative slices: short chat, long-form generation, multi-turn dialog with context reuse, and embedding-only workloads.
3) Golden Prompt Bank & evals: curated ~400 prompts across categories (QA, instruction, summarization, code, safety edge cases). Quality metrics: instruction-following score (automated rubric), semantic similarity (embedding cosine to golden responses), log-likelihood delta, and a small human eval subset for calibration.
4) Intervention simulator: orchestration layer that applies policy matrix (alert triggers + actions) and simulates the downstream actions (scale up, throttle, rollback, route to fallback model). Outputs: TP/FP/FN/TN for policy, mean time-to-detect, mean time-to-restoration, and projected cost delta.
5) Dashboards & artifacts: Grafana dashboard for simulated runs, an evaluation notebook (Colab/Drive) with side-by-side LQ plots, and a Confluence playbook for on-call steps.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulator can run 5 canonical scenarios end-to-end on CI (runs in <2h with sampled workload) and produce an artifacts bundle with latency histograms, quality deltas, and policy confusion matrix.
- Playbook includes at least 3 policy templates (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with explicit numeric thresholds and example runbooks.
- Demo run using historical incident X (see incident link) reproduces the detection behavior and recommends the same rollback in >80% of trials.

Risk/Trade-offs:
- Synthetic workloads may under/over-estimate quality regressions; we mitigate by calibrating with human evals and using historical incidents as ground truth.
- Strict automated rollback policies can cause churn; simulator will compute expected churn rate and FP risk so SRE can choose appropriate safety margins.
